jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: The Art of Letting Go
jokes.joke: I downloaded a meditation app to help me stay calm. It promised a free trial, then charged me $200. I called for a refund, and a soothing voice said, 'Breathe. Notice your anger. Let it go.' I said, 'You stole my money!' It said, 'And yet you're still so attached to it.'

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: The Calmest I’ve Ever Been
jokes.joke: I got a call last month saying my car’s extended warranty was expiring, and I have never felt more at peace in my life. My voice got slow, my shoulders dropped, I started breathing from my diaphragm. The guy said, ‘Sir, is now a good time?’ I said, ‘Honestly? Yeah.’ I don’t know what that says about my actual life, but the one time a stranger lied to my face and tried to take my money, I finally found my center.

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Grief Upcharge
jokes.joke: I got scammed at a funeral home last week, which feels like the least sporting venue to run a hustle. The director sat me down in a velvet room, nodded very gently, and said, "We have the pine box, or the Eternal Serenity Mahogany with memory-foam lining." I looked at him and said, "Buddy, he's dead. If he starts complaining about lumbar support, we've got way bigger problems than our budget."

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Soft-Spoken Sendoff
jokes.joke: I'm a funeral director, but I'm painfully timid. Last week a widow asked if her husband looked peaceful. I stared at my shoes for a full ten seconds and finally muttered, 'Well... he hasn't complained yet.' Then I quietly excused myself to go straighten flowers that were already perfect.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Final Expense
jokes.joke: I knew I'd been scammed when a funeral director sold me a 'lifetime burial package.' Halfway through the paperwork I said, 'Lifetime? Isn't every burial package lifetime?' He smiled and said, 'Exactly. That's why it's our longest-lasting product.'

scores.comment: An amusing contrast between serenity and a scam call, but the extended setup leads to an observation rather than a strong punchline. The final sentence explains the premise instead of delivering a laugh.

A recognizable funeral-home upselling premise with effective escalation. The lumbar-support punchline is concrete, accessible, and well timed. The underlying observation is familiar, but the execution delivers a genuine laugh.
The timid characterization is clear, but 'he hasn't complained yet' is a predictable dead-person joke. The closing flower-straightening detail adds characterization without strengthening the payoff.

Concise and understandable, but the lifetime-burial observation is apparent almost immediately. The director's response merely repeats the central irony rather than introducing a surprising comic turn.
Clean irony with meditation-app voice; solid final line, slightly familiar app-bot gag shape.

Mild and cute, but the timid-undertaker bit stays flat; punchline restates premise rather than turning it.

Clean first-person setup and crisp final turn using the meditation app framing well, though the 'attached to your money' angle is somewhat familiar.
Fresh reversal on finding zen during a scam call; the ending trails off slightly into explanation rather than snapping on a sharp punchline.

Clever mindfulness reversal, but therapy-flavored and mild; more admire than laugh.
Strong inversion of the scam call into unexpected calm; clean stage voice and solid closer.

Strong personification of the app; the attachment line is a solid turn and punchline.
